```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
codes <- readr::read_csv("coding/round2_codes_long.csv")
interviews <- readr::read_csv("coding/round2_interviews.csv")
```

## Purpose of this note

This note summarises the second round of coding for the interviews
with volunteers and coordinators at community food projects. It is
meant for the project team, not for publication. Quotes are included
to give a flavour of each theme; full extracts are in the NVivo file.

In total we coded `r nrow(interviews)` interviews, with a median
length of `r median(interviews$duration_min)` minutes. Two coders
(MF and GP) coded every transcript independently, then met to resolve
disagreements.

## Agreement

```{r kappa}
k <- irr::kappa2(codes[, c("coder_mf", "coder_gp")])
```

Cohen's κ across all codes was `r round(k$value, 2)` before
reconciliation. Agreement was lowest for the *stigma* and *dignity*
codes, which overlap a great deal; we have since merged them (see
below).

## Changes to the codebook

The following changes were agreed at the reconciliation meeting:

1. *Stigma* and *dignity* merged into a single parent code,
   **dignity and stigma**, with two children.
2. New code *infrastructure* for talk about buildings, fridges, vans
   and storage. To check how often it was applied:

   ```{r infra-count}
   codes |> filter(code == "infrastructure") |> count(interview_id)
   ```

3. *Volunteer burnout* split into *burnout* and *turnover*, since
   participants clearly treated these as different problems.
4. Retired codes are kept in the codebook with a note, so the round 1
   coding can still be read.

## Themes

### Dignity and stigma

The most frequently applied code. Coordinators described a range of
practices intended to make the projects feel less like charity:

- letting people choose items rather than receiving a fixed parcel;
- running the project alongside a café or social meal;
- avoiding asking for proof of need.

> We don't ask for referral slips any more. People were embarrassed to
> bring them, and honestly it didn't stop anyone who didn't need it,
> because almost nobody comes here who doesn't need it. (Coordinator,
> project 04)

### Infrastructure

Talk about physical infrastructure came up far more than we expected.
Almost every coordinator raised storage, and particularly cold
storage, as a constraint on what they could accept from donors.

```{r fig-infra, fig.cap="Interviews mentioning each infrastructure sub-code.", fig.height=3.5}
codes |>
  filter(parent == "infrastructure") |>
  count(code) |>
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(n, reorder(code, n))) +
  ggplot2::geom_col() +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Interviews", y = NULL)
```

### Burnout and turnover

Burnout was mostly discussed by long-standing volunteers, turnover by
coordinators. Several described a "core" of two or three people
holding the project together.
